# Open3DJ DSL reference

<!-- Generated by packages/mcp/src/dsl-docs.ts from DSL_ENTRIES in @open3dj/dsl. Do not edit by hand: run node packages/mcp/src/dsl-docs.ts --write. -->

DSL v1 is a 3dj-compatible modelling surface for scripts. This page is what the `docs` tool searches. Sections: Basics, DSL reference (starting with All entries), Standard parts (lib), Later entries, Error playbook, Examples and Gallery examples.

## Basics

### Units, axes and return values

Units are millimetres and Z is up. Angles are degrees. A script is plain JavaScript that ends with a return:

- `return shape`: one part.
- `return [{ name: "Base", shape: base, color: "#5b6b7a" }, { name: "Lid", shape: lid }]`: several parts.
- `return { Base: base, Lid: lid }`: several parts named by the keys.

Every design is an assembly: a single part is an assembly with one occurrence. Parts with the same name get #n suffixes (screw#1, screw#2), and moved clones share one definition.

### Getting started: the tool loop

1. `docs {query: "fillet"}` to look up an entry; `docs {query: "entries"}` lists them all.
2. `run {project: "bracket.o3j", script}` returns a GeometryReport: validity, volume, bbox and counts per definition, clashes and contacts between parts, and next steps. Keep the `rev` it returns.
3. `render {project, view: "multiview"}` returns a four-view drawing (PNG, or SVG with format svg).
4. `export {project, format: "step"}` writes STEP, STL, glTF (.glb) or 3MF under out/<rev>/ with an evidence sidecar.
5. Change the script and `run` again with `base_rev` set to the last rev. A stale base_rev returns REV_CONFLICT.

The CLI does the same: `open3dj run part.o3j.js`, `open3dj render part.o3j`, `open3dj export part.o3j --format step`.

### Sandbox limits

Scripts run in a QuickJS sandbox with no file system, network, timers or Date. Math.random is seeded. Limits: 2 s of script CPU time (kernel time excluded), 128 MiB of memory, 5000 kernel calls and 20000 live shapes per run, and at most 1000 items in one list argument (split longer lists into several calls). console.log output is kept with the run, never printed to the MCP stream.

## DSL reference

### All entries

An overview of every entry in this version. `docs {query: "<name>"}` gives the signature and an example.

Shapes, profiles and operations: `Param.number`, `Param.bool`, `Param.choice`, `Param.string`, `box`, `cylinder`, `sphere`, `torus`, `rect`, `roundedRect`, `circle2d`, `ellipse`, `ngon`, `star`, `slot`, `polygon`, `path`, `sketch.extrude`, `sketch.revolve`, `sketch.loftTo`, `loft`, `sketch.offset`, `sketch.filletCorners`, `sketch.chamferCorners`, `sketch.transform`, `sketch.boolean`, `sketch.measure`, `add`, `subtract`, `intersect`, `cutPlane`, `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, `mirror`, `pointAlong`, `moveTo`, `clone`, `fillet`, `chamfer`, `shell`, `edges`, `linearPattern`, `circularPattern`, `mirrorCopy`, `measure`, `color`, `name`, `withReferences`, `attachTo`, `connector`, `withConnectors`, `matchTo`.

Standard parts: `lib.fastener`, `lib.clearanceHole`, `lib.screwCutter`, `lib.heatSetPocket`, `lib.hexNutPocket`, `lib.bolt`, `lib.nut`, `lib.washer`.

### Param.number

```js
Param.number(name, default, { min, max, step, unit, integer })
```

A number parameter; caller values override the default and are clamped to min and max.

Example:

```js
const width = Param.number("Width", 40, { min: 20, max: 120, unit: "mm" });
return box(width, 20, 5);
```

### Param.bool

```js
Param.bool(name, default)
```

A true/false parameter.

Example:

```js
const holes = Param.bool("Holes", true);
const plate = box(40, 20, 5);
return holes ? plate.subtract(cylinder(7, 3).translate(0, 0, -1)) : plate;
```

### Param.choice

```js
Param.choice(name, default, [options])
```

One of a list of values.

Example:

```js
const size = Param.choice("Size", "M4", ["M3", "M4", "M5"]);
return box(30, 30, 6).subtract(lib.clearanceHole(size, { length: 7 }).translateZ(6));
```

### Param.string

```js
Param.string(name, default, { maxLength })
```

A text parameter.

Example:

```js
const label = Param.string("Label", "A", { maxLength: 8 });
return box(10, 10, label.length + 2);
```

### box

```js
box(width, depth, height)
```

Box centred on XY with its base on Z = 0.

Example:

```js
return box(40, 20, 10); // x from -20 to 20, y from -10 to 10, z from 0 to 10
```

### cylinder

```js
cylinder(height, radius, radiusTop?)
```

Cylinder on Z from 0 to height; radiusTop makes a cone.

Example:

```js
return cylinder(30, 8).add(cylinder(10, 12, 8).translateZ(30)); // a post with a cone on top
```

### sphere

```js
sphere(radius)
```

Sphere centred on the origin.

Example:

```js
return sphere(10).cutPlane("XY", 0, "positive"); // a dome
```

### torus

```js
torus(majorRadius, minorRadius)
```

Torus in the XY plane.

Example:

```js
return torus(20, 3);
```

### rect

```js
rect(w, h)
```

Rectangle profile centred on the origin.

Example:

```js
return rect(30, 20).extrude(4);
```

### roundedRect

```js
roundedRect(w, h, r)
```

Rectangle profile with rounded corners.

Example:

```js
return roundedRect(60, 40, 6).extrude(3);
```

### circle2d

```js
circle2d(r)
```

Circle profile.

Example:

```js
return circle2d(10).extrude(2);
```

### ellipse

```js
ellipse(rx, ry)
```

Ellipse profile with an exact curve. Sketch booleans keep the exact curve; corner fillets and chamfers on it use a close B-spline approximation.

Example:

```js
return ellipse(12, 6).extrude(3);
```

### ngon

```js
ngon(sides, radius)
```

Regular polygon profile; radius is the circumradius.

Example:

```js
return ngon(6, 10).extrude(5).subtract(cylinder(7, 3).translate(0, 0, -1)); // a hex nut blank
```

### star

```js
star(points, outerR, innerR)
```

Star profile.

Example:

```js
return star(5, 20, 8).extrude(3);
```

### slot

```js
slot(length, width)
```

Stadium-shaped slot profile.

Example:

```js
return box(50, 20, 4).subtract(slot(30, 6).extrude(6).translateZ(-1));
```

### polygon

```js
polygon([[x, y], ...])
```

Closed polygon profile; duplicate points are removed.

Example:

```js
return polygon([[0, 0], [40, 0], [40, 5], [5, 30], [0, 30]]).extrude(8);
```

### path

```js
path().moveTo(x,y).lineTo(x,y).lineH(dx).lineV(dy).lineAngled(len,deg).arcTo(x,y,r).close()
```

Profile drawn segment by segment; arcTo with positive r bulges to the left of travel.

Example:

```js
const profile = path().moveTo(0, 0).lineH(30).lineV(10).arcTo(20, 20, 10).lineTo(0, 20).close();
return profile.extrude(5);
```

### sketch.extrude

```js
sketch.extrude(h, { twist, scaleTop })
```

Extrude a profile along +Z, optionally twisted (degrees) and tapered.

Example:

```js
return ngon(6, 15).extrude(40, { twist: 60, scaleTop: 0.6 });
```

### sketch.revolve

```js
sketch.revolve(deg = 360)
```

Revolve about Z; sketch X is the radius and sketch Y the height.

Example:

```js
return rect(4, 10).translate(12, 5).revolve(); // a ring, inner radius 10, outer 14
```

### sketch.loftTo

```js
sketch.loftTo(other, h)
```

Loft from this profile at Z = 0 to other at Z = h.

Example:

```js
return rect(30, 30).loftTo(circle2d(8), 25);
```

### loft

```js
loft([profiles], [heights])
```

Loft through profiles placed at the given heights.

Example:

```js
return loft([rect(30, 30), circle2d(12), rect(10, 10)], [0, 15, 30]);
```

### sketch.offset

```js
sketch.offset(d)
```

Exact 2D offset (positive grows); later edits use the kernel profile.

Example:

```js
return roundedRect(40, 20, 4).offset(2).extrude(3);
```

### sketch.filletCorners

```js
sketch.filletCorners(r)
```

Round every corner of the profile: drawn profiles, and kernel profiles after offset or a sketch boolean (there, a corner is where the outline turns; smooth joins stay as they are).

Example:

```js
return rect(40, 20).filletCorners(5).extrude(3);
```

### sketch.chamferCorners

```js
sketch.chamferCorners(s)
```

Chamfer every corner of the profile, drawn or after offset or a sketch boolean.

Example:

```js
return rect(40, 20).chamferCorners(3).extrude(3);
```

### sketch.transform

```js
sketch.translate(x, y) .rotate(deg) .scale(f) .mirror([nx, ny])
```

2D transforms; mirror takes the normal of the mirror line through the origin.

Example:

```js
return rect(10, 4).translate(10, 0).rotate(45).extrude(2);
```

### sketch.boolean

```js
sketch.add/.subtract/.intersect(...), union2d/difference2d/intersection2d
```

2D booleans, computed by the kernel, so curved outlines and holes are exact. The result is a kernel profile: transform, offset, filletCorners, chamferCorners, extrude and revolve it as usual.

Example:

```js
return rect(40, 20).subtract(circle2d(5).translate(10, 0)).extrude(3);
```

### sketch.measure

```js
sketch.area() .bounds()
```

Area and 2D bounds of a profile.

Example:

```js
const s = roundedRect(40, 20, 4);
console.log(s.area(), JSON.stringify(s.bounds()));
return s.extrude(1);
```

### add

```js
a.add(b, ...) / union(...)
```

Batched union (one fuseAll).

Example:

```js
return box(40, 10, 5).add(box(10, 40, 5), cylinder(10, 4)); // one fused solid
```

### subtract

```js
a.subtract(b, ...) / difference(a, ...)
```

Batched subtraction (one cutAll).

Example:

```js
const holes = [-12, 0, 12].map((x) => cylinder(7, 2).translate(x, 0, -1));
return box(40, 10, 5).subtract(holes);
```

### intersect

```js
a.intersect(b, ...) / intersection(...)
```

Intersection.

Example:

```js
return box(20, 20, 20).intersect(sphere(13));
```

### cutPlane

```js
shape.cutPlane(plane = 'XY', offset = 0, keep = 'positive')
```

Keep one side of an axis plane.

Example:

```js
return sphere(10).cutPlane("XY", 2, "negative"); // keep z below 2
```

### translate

```js
.translate(x, y, z) .translateX/Y/Z(d) .translatePolar(r, deg, z)
```

Move a shape.

Example:

```js
return box(10, 10, 10).translate(20, 0, 0).translateZ(5);
```

### rotate

```js
.rotate([ax, ay, az], deg, pivot | { pivot }) .rotateX/Y/Z(deg) .rotateAroundAxis(axis, deg, pivot)
```

Rotate a shape (degrees, right-hand rule).

Example:

```js
return box(30, 4, 4).rotate([0, 0, 1], 45).rotateX(10);
```

### scale

```js
.scale(f)
```

Uniform scale about the origin.

Example:

```js
return sphere(5).scale(2);
```

### mirror

```js
.mirror([nx, ny, nz]) .mirrorThrough(point, normal)
```

Reflect through a plane given by its normal.

Example:

```js
return box(10, 10, 10).translate(15, 0, 0).mirror([1, 0, 0]); // now at x = -15
```

### pointAlong

```js
.pointAlong([x, y, z])
```

Lay the shape's +Z axis along a direction.

Example:

```js
return cylinder(30, 2).pointAlong([1, 0, 0]); // the axis now runs along X
```

### moveTo

```js
.moveTo(x, y, z)
```

Put the bounding-box min corner at a point.

Example:

```js
return box(10, 10, 10).moveTo(0, 0, 0); // min corner at the origin
```

### clone

```js
.clone() .duplicate()
```

A rigid copy; moved clones share one definition in the assembly.

Example:

```js
const leg = cylinder(30, 3);
return [
  { name: "Leg 1", shape: leg.clone().translate(-20, -20, 0) },
  { name: "Leg 2", shape: leg.clone().translate(20, -20, 0) },
  { name: "Leg 3", shape: leg.clone().translate(0, 20, 0) },
];
```

### fillet

```js
fillet(shape, r, edgeQuery?)
```

Round edges; edgeQuery { atZ, atX, atY, parallel, perpendicular, minLength, maxLength }.

Example:

```js
return fillet(box(40, 30, 10), 2, { atZ: 10 }); // round the four top edges
```

### chamfer

```js
chamfer(shape, size, edgeQuery?)
```

Chamfer edges.

Example:

```js
return chamfer(box(40, 30, 10), 1, { parallel: [0, 0, 1] }); // break the vertical edges
```

### shell

```js
shape.shell(t, { openTop = true, openBottom = false })
```

Hollow with walls inside the skin. When the kernel cannot, a straight extrusion falls back to a profile offset, as long as it was only moved or turned about Z: shell before other rotations.

Example:

```js
return roundedRect(60, 40, 5).extrude(25).shell(2); // open-top tray, 2 mm walls inside the skin
```

### edges

```js
shape.edges(edgeQuery?)
```

List the edges a query matches (index, curve, length, start, end). Open3DJ extension.

Example:

```js
console.log(JSON.stringify(box(20, 20, 10).edges({ atZ: 10 }).map((e) => e.length)));
return box(20, 20, 10);
```

### linearPattern

```js
linearPattern(shape, count, dx, dy, dz?)
```

Copies along a vector, unioned.

Example:

```js
return box(44, 8, 2).add(linearPattern(cylinder(8, 2).translate(-16, 0, 0), 5, 8, 0)); // five pins, 8 mm apart, on a strip
```

### circularPattern

```js
circularPattern(shape, count, { centerX, centerY, startDeg, angle })
```

Copies around Z, unioned.

Example:

```js
return box(40, 40, 3).subtract(circularPattern(cylinder(5, 2).translate(14, 0, -1), 6));
```

### mirrorCopy

```js
mirrorCopy(shape, [nx, ny, nz])
```

Shape plus its reflection through the origin plane.

Example:

```js
return box(20, 10, 5).add(mirrorCopy(box(10, 10, 5).translate(15, 0, 0), [1, 0, 0])); // a 40 mm bar built from one half
```

### measure

```js
shape.volume() .area() .bounds() .geometryInfo()
```

Volume, area, { min, max, size, center }, and solid/face/edge counts with validity.

Example:

```js
const part = box(20, 10, 5);
console.log(part.volume(), part.area(), JSON.stringify(part.bounds().size), JSON.stringify(part.geometryInfo()));
return part;
```

### color

```js
.color('#rrggbb')
```

Part colour.

Example:

```js
return box(20, 20, 5).color("#00d4ff");
```

### name

```js
.name('Base')
```

Part name.

Example:

```js
return box(20, 20, 5).name("Base plate");
```

### withReferences

```js
.withReferences({ name: [x, y, z] | { face: query } | { edge: query } }) .referenceNames() .referencePoint(name) .placeReference(name, [x, y, z])
```

Named points that follow the shape through transforms, and named faces and edges. A face query takes normal, surface, atX, atY, atZ, minArea, maxArea and near; an edge query takes the edge query fields plus curve and near. near keeps the matches closest to the point, measured from the point to the face or edge itself (not to its centroid, which lies on the axis of a cylinder, cone or torus face). Each named face or edge gets a geometric fingerprint, and the report's refs say after every run whether the name is exact, ambiguous (with candidates, never auto-picked) or broken (with a reason). Name faces before moving or turning the whole part: the next run compares fingerprints in the frame the name was given in, so a new placement keeps names exact. A named element with an identical twin (one hole of a symmetric pair) stays exact only at its position or on its plane or axis; when the twins move with a parameter it is ambiguous, with the query's pick as candidates[0].

Example:

```js
const plate = box(40, 20, 5).withReferences({ hole: [10, 0, 5] }).translate(0, 0, 10);
const [x, y, z] = plate.referencePoint("hole");
const drilled = plate.subtract(cylinder(10, 2).translate(x, y, z - 7));
// Name a face and an edge on the final shape: refs[] in the report says whether later runs still find them.
return drilled.withReferences({ top: { face: { normal: [0, 0, 1], atZ: 15 } }, bore: { face: { surface: "cylinder" } }, front_top: { edge: { parallel: [1, 0, 0], atY: -10, atZ: 15 } } });
```

### attachTo

```js
child.attachTo(parent, parentAnchor, myAnchor, offset?)
```

Move so that two anchors meet; anchors are references or top bottom left right front back center.

Example:

```js
const base = box(40, 40, 10);
const knob = cylinder(8, 6).attachTo(base, "top", "bottom");
return [{ name: "Base", shape: base }, { name: "Knob", shape: knob }];
```

### connector

```js
connector.male/female(type, { origin, axis, up })
```

A connector frame.

Example:

```js
const seat = connector.female("seat", { origin: [0, 0, 5], axis: [0, 0, 1], up: [1, 0, 0] });
return box(20, 20, 5).withConnectors({ seat });
```

### withConnectors

```js
.withConnectors({ name: connector })
```

Attach connectors to a part.

Example:

```js
const plate = box(30, 30, 4).withConnectors({
  top: connector.female("seat", { origin: [0, 0, 4], axis: [0, 0, 1], up: [1, 0, 0] }),
});
return plate;
```

### matchTo

```js
moving.matchTo(target, movingName, targetName)
```

Seat the male connector on the female one (axes anti-aligned) and record a fastened mate.

Example:

```js
const base = box(30, 30, 4).withConnectors({ top: connector.female("seat", { origin: [0, 0, 4], axis: [0, 0, 1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) });
const post = cylinder(20, 3).withConnectors({ foot: connector.male("seat", { origin: [0, 0, 0], axis: [0, 0, -1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) });
return [{ name: "Base", shape: base }, { name: "Post", shape: post.matchTo(base, "foot", "top") }];
```

## Standard parts (lib)

Dimensions come from public tables of ISO 273, ISO 4762, ISO 10642, ISO 4032 and ISO 7089; heat-set pockets use typical values, not a standard. Hardware is schematic, without threads.

### lib.fastener

```js
lib.fastener('M3')
```

Metric fastener data M2 to M8 (ISO 273, 4762, 10642, 4032, 7089).

Example:

```js
const f = lib.fastener("M4");
console.log(JSON.stringify(f));
return box(20, 20, 5);
```

### lib.clearanceHole

```js
lib.clearanceHole(size, { length, fit })
```

ISO 273 clearance hole cutter from Z = 0 down.

Example:

```js
return box(30, 30, 6).subtract(lib.clearanceHole("M4", { length: 7 }).translateZ(6));
```

### lib.screwCutter

```js
lib.screwCutter(size, { length, head, clearance })
```

Screw cutter with socket, countersunk or no head.

Example:

```js
return box(30, 30, 8).subtract(lib.screwCutter("M3", { head: "countersunk", length: 10 }).translateZ(8));
```

### lib.heatSetPocket

```js
lib.heatSetPocket(size, { depth, clearance })
```

Pocket for a heat-set insert (typical sizes, not a standard).

Example:

```js
return cylinder(12, 5).subtract(lib.heatSetPocket("M3").translateZ(12));
```

### lib.hexNutPocket

```js
lib.hexNutPocket(size, { depth, clearance })
```

Hexagon pocket for an ISO 4032 nut.

Example:

```js
return box(20, 20, 8).subtract(lib.hexNutPocket("M4", { depth: 4 }).translateZ(8));
```

### lib.bolt

```js
lib.bolt(size, length)
```

Schematic ISO 4762 socket head cap screw; head above Z = 0.

Example:

```js
return lib.bolt("M5", 20); // head above z = 0, shank below
```

### lib.nut

```js
lib.nut(size)
```

Schematic ISO 4032 nut centred on the origin.

Example:

```js
return lib.nut("M5");
```

### lib.washer

```js
lib.washer(size)
```

ISO 7089 washer centred on the origin.

Example:

```js
return lib.washer("M5");
```

## Later entries

### Planned for later steps

These 3dj entries throw DSL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED in S1. Build the same shape from the entries above.

- `text2d(str, { size })`: Text profile.
- `spline2d(points, { closed })`: Spline profile.
- `child.onFace(parent, face, { u, v, protrude })`: Place on a face.
- `shape.hole(face, { diameter, ... })`: Holes with counterbores and countersinks.
- `shape.cutout(sketch.onFace(...), { depth })`: Pocket from a sketch on a face.
- `group(a, b, ...)`: Keep parts separate as a group.
- `tolerance(shape, mm)`: Exact offset cutter.
- `chamferBottomEdges(shape, size)`: Elephant-foot chamfer.
- `minWall(shape, mm)`: Wall thickness screen.
- `lib.snapFit, lib.screwBoss, lib.mountingTab, lib.cableAnchor, lib.remoteCradle, lib.profile2020BSlot6, lib.tSlotProfile`: More library content.

## Error playbook

Errors come back as tool results with status error and an error object: code, message, line and column in the script, op, faulty elements (edge:3, face:2) and a hint. The CLI exits with 2 for these.

### SCRIPT_SYNTAX

The script is not valid JavaScript. line and column point at the problem.

Fix: Fix the syntax at that line. Scripts are plain JavaScript (ES2023) without import or require.

### SCRIPT_RUNTIME

The script threw an error, for example a TypeError from a misspelt method.

Fix: Read the message at the reported line. docs {query: "<entry>"} shows the right signature.

### SCRIPT_TIMEOUT

The script used more than its CPU budget (2 s by default, kernel time excluded) or ran into the wall-clock limit. Catching the interrupt (for example inside an async function) does not help: the run still ends with this code.

Fix: Remove loops that build many shapes one by one; pass arrays to add and subtract so the kernel runs one batched boolean.

### SCRIPT_MEMORY

The script used more than its memory cap (128 MiB).

Fix: Build fewer temporary arrays and strings; geometry itself lives in the kernel and does not count.

### SCRIPT_STACK

Recursion went too deep.

Fix: Replace deep recursion with a loop.

### SCRIPT_LIMIT

A budget ran out: host calls (5000), live shapes (20000), items in one list argument (1000) or string length.

Fix: Too many calls: batch work (one subtract with an array instead of a loop of subtracts) and do not create shapes you do not use. Too many items in one list ("over the batch limit"): split the list into calls of at most 1000 items and combine the results.

### SCRIPT_RESULT_TOO_LARGE

The returned value is larger than 64 KiB of plain data.

Fix: Return shapes and short names, not large arrays of numbers.

### SCRIPT_NO_RESULT

The script did not return anything.

Fix: End with return shape, return [{ name, shape }] or return { Name: shape }.

### SCRIPT_CANCELLED

The run was cancelled before it finished.

Fix: Run again if the cancel was not intended.

### HOST_ERROR

A host function failed in an unexpected way.

Fix: Simplify the failing call. If it repeats with valid input, report it with the script.

### DSL_BAD_ARGUMENT

An entry got an argument of the wrong type or range, for example a negative box size.

Fix: Check the entry's signature with docs {query: "<entry>"}; sizes are positive millimetres, angles are degrees.

### DSL_BAD_HANDLE

A shape or sketch handle is not valid any more, for example from an earlier run.

Fix: Build every shape inside the script that returns it.

### DSL_BAD_PARAM

A Param definition or a caller value is wrong, for example a choice that is not in the list.

Fix: Use a value from the options, or fix the Param call at the reported line.

### DSL_BAD_RETURN

The returned value is not a shape, a list of { name, shape } or an object of shapes.

Fix: Return shapes, [{ name, shape, color? }] or { Name: shape }.

### DSL_NO_EDGES

An edge query for fillet or chamfer matched no edge.

Fix: List the edges with shape.edges() and console.log, then narrow or widen the query (atZ, parallel, minLength).

### DSL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED

The entry exists in the 3dj DSL but arrives in a later Open3DJ step.

Fix: Build the same shape from implemented entries. docs lists what is available.

### DSL_UNKNOWN_ANCHOR

attachTo got an anchor name that is neither a reference nor top, bottom, left, right, front, back or center.

Fix: Use a built-in anchor or add the point with withReferences.

### DSL_MISSING_CONNECTOR

matchTo named a connector the shape does not have.

Fix: Attach it first with withConnectors({ name: connector.male(...) }).

### DSL_EMPTY_RESULT

A part has no solid left, usually because a cut removed everything. line points at the call that made the part.

Fix: Check the cutter size and position (cutters bigger than the part remove it all), or render the parts before the cut.

### BAD_PART

A returned part is not a usable shape: it could not be measured, for example a surface or a broken result. line points at the call that made it.

Fix: Return solids. Render the parts before the last operation to see what it did.

### DSL_UNSUPPORTED

The combination of options is not supported, for example offset on a profile with holes, or a 2D boolean or corner fillet whose result fails its area check.

Fix: Follow the hint; usually build the profile in two steps, or extrude the profiles and combine the solids.

### DSL_OVERLAPPING_SOLIDS

One returned part holds several solids that share volume, so its volume and mass would be counted twice.

Fix: Union the pieces into one solid (a.union(b)), or return them as separate parts.

### KERNEL_BOOLEAN_FAILED

OCCT could not compute a union, cut or intersection.

Fix: Make tools overlap the body clearly and avoid coincident faces: extend cutters 0.01 mm or more past the faces they cut.

### KERNEL_FILLET_FAILED

OCCT could not round the chosen edges. elements names them (edge:N).

Fix: Use a smaller radius, or fillet fewer edges at once; fillet before boolean cuts that meet the edge.

### KERNEL_CHAMFER_FAILED

OCCT could not chamfer the chosen edges.

Fix: Use a smaller size or fewer edges.

### KERNEL_SHELL_FAILED

OCCT could not hollow the solid.

Fix: Use a thinner wall, or shell before adding fillets (keep corner radii larger than the wall).

### KERNEL_INVALID_RESULT

An operation returned a shape that is not a valid solid, or a shell that is wrong although valid. elements names faulty faces.

Fix: Follow the hint. For shell: thinner walls, or shell first and fillet after.

### KERNEL_NOT_A_SOLID

A feature needs one solid but got several bodies or a surface.

Fix: Union the bodies first, or apply the feature to each body.

### KERNEL_CONSTRUCTION_FAILED

A primitive or profile could not be built, for example a zero-size box or a self-crossing polygon.

Fix: Check sizes and point order.

### KERNEL_BAD_ARGUMENT

The kernel refused an argument, for example a size that is not a finite number.

Fix: Check the numbers passed at the reported line; docs {query: "<entry>"} gives the ranges.

### KERNEL_INVALID_HANDLE

A shape handle was used after the kernel released it. This is a bug in Open3DJ, not in the script.

Fix: Run again; if it repeats, report it with the script.

### KERNEL_TESSELLATION_FAILED

The kernel could not mesh a part for a render or a mesh export (STL, glTF, 3MF).

Fix: Look for tiny or sliver faces near the last operation (very small fillets, nearly tangent cuts) and simplify them; STEP export does not need a mesh.

### KERNEL_IO_FAILED

The kernel could not write or read a STEP, STL or BREP form of the shape.

Fix: Check that the part is valid in the report; if it is and this repeats, report it with the script.

### KERNEL_HEALING_FAILED

The kernel could not repair a shape.

Fix: Simplify the operation named in op; report it if it repeats.

### KERNEL_UNKNOWN

The kernel failed without a known cause.

Fix: Simplify the operation named in op and run again; report it with the script if it repeats.

### KERNEL_KERNEL_ABORT

The kernel aborted. The worker is replaced, so the next call starts clean.

Fix: Simplify the operation named in op; report it if it repeats.

### BAD_TRANSFORM

A part's placement is not a rigid move (its rotation is not a unit quaternion).

Fix: Place parts with translate, rotate and matchTo; do not scale a clone.

### UNKNOWN_DEFINITION

An occurrence uses a definition with no geometry. This is a bug in Open3DJ, not in the script.

Fix: Run the script again; if it repeats, report it with the script.

### ASSEMBLY_TOO_DEEP

Sub-assemblies nest deeper than 32 levels.

Fix: Flatten the grouping: fewer levels of nested groups.

### ASSEMBLY_TOO_LARGE

The previous revision's assembly graph expands to more than 100000 occurrences, which Open3DJ never writes; the project files were changed outside Open3DJ.

Fix: Restore the revision from git, or run the script in a fresh project.

### XCAF_LOCATION_MISMATCH

The STEP writer stored a different placement for an occurrence than the assembly holds. This is a bug in Open3DJ.

Fix: Export STL, glTF or 3MF meanwhile, and report it with the script.

### BAD_FORMAT

An export or render format is not one of the supported ones.

Fix: Export step, stl, gltf or 3mf; render png, svg or both.

### BAD_OPTION

An export option is out of range, for example a mesh deflection of 0.

Fix: Leave the option out to use the default.

### BAD_SIZE

A render width or height is not a whole number of pixels in the allowed range.

Fix: Leave the size out, or use a value from the message's range.

### UNSUPPORTED_VIEW

The render view is not available yet.

Fix: Use view "multiview".

### UNKNOWN_TARGET

A target or scope names no occurrence, sub-assembly or definition.

Fix: Use inspect {fields: ["tree"]} to list paths such as lid, screw#2 or pcb_assy/standoff#1.

### EMPTY_ASSEMBLY

The script returned no parts.

Fix: Return at least one shape.

### REV_CONFLICT

base_rev is an older revision, not the project's head: another change landed first. Nothing was changed. (A base_rev that never existed is UNKNOWN_REV.)

Fix: inspect the head revision, then run again with base_rev set to it (or omit base_rev to build on the head).

### UNKNOWN_REV

The rev or base_rev does not exist in this project, for example a typo or a rev ahead of the head.

Fix: Use a rev from an earlier result; the message names the head and the hint lists known revisions.

### NO_REVISION

The project has no revision or no script yet.

Fix: Call run with a script first.

### PROJECT_NOT_FOUND

The project folder has no project.o3j.json.

Fix: Call run with a script; it creates the project.

### PROJECT_PATH

The project path is not a folder whose name ends in .o3j, its parent folder does not exist, or a part of the path is a file (the message gives the file system code, such as ENOTDIR).

Fix: Use a project directly in the folder the server runs in, such as bracket.o3j, or inside a folder that already exists there.

### PATH_REFUSED

A path would leave the project or server folder, is absolute, goes through a symlink, or names the store's own files (revisions, .o3j-cache, .o3j-lock, project.o3j.json and the other project files).

Fix: Use a relative path inside the project, such as exports or out/r_0002.

### PROJECT_CORRUPT

A project file is not valid JSON or does not match its schema, a revision's assembly graph is too large to be one Open3DJ wrote (more than 100000 occurrences or 32 levels), or something other than a lock file sits at .o3j-lock.

Fix: Fix or delete the named file or folder by hand, or restore it from git.

### PROJECT_REQUIRED

inspect fields tree, refs, fits and measure need a project.

Fix: Pass project; devices and job work without one.

### OP_NOT_IMPLEMENTED

The run op arrives in a later step: add_occurrence, remove, set_transform and replace_definition come in S2. S1 supports set_param and cancel_job.

Fix: Change the script so it returns the parts with their placements, and run it again.

### PROJECT_BUSY

Another process (a second daemon or the CLI) held the project's lock file for more than 15 s.

Fix: Run again. If no other open3dj process runs, delete the project's .o3j-lock file.

### STEP_HEADER

The STEP writer produced a file without the HEADER section or FILE_SCHEMA that Open3DJ rewrites with the file name, author and version.

Fix: Report it with the script: the kernel's STEP writer changed. STL, glTF and 3MF still work.

### STEP_ROUNDTRIP_FAILED

The STEP file did not re-import as the same solids (count, validity or volume), so other CAD tools would open a broken part. The message names the occurrence and faces.

Fix: Usually a revolved profile whose end meets the axis at an angle: end it square to the axis (an arc centred on the axis, or a short flat). A curve the STEP writer cannot express (an offset of a spline) is the other known cause: simplify that profile. STL, glTF and 3MF still work.

### BAD_INPUT

The tool input does not match the tool's input schema.

Fix: Check the schema in tools/list; the message names the field.

### NO_BACKEND

compute asked for gpu or cloud, which arrive in later steps.

Fix: Use compute "auto" or "cpu".

### JOB_TIMEOUT

The job ran past the pool's wall-clock limit and its worker was stopped.

Fix: Simplify the script or split it into parts.

### JOB_MEMORY

The job needed more kernel memory than a worker may use (2 GiB by default), so the worker was stopped and replaced.

Fix: Make the part smaller or simpler (fewer patterned features), or split it into parts. Sizes are in mm.

### JOB_CANCELLED

The job was cancelled with run ops=[{op: "cancel_job"}]. No revision was created.

Fix: Run again if needed.

### JOB_NOT_FOUND

No job with that id in this daemon. Jobs are kept in memory only.

Fix: Run again; a restarted daemon forgets its jobs.

### WORKER_CRASHED

The worker running the job died and was replaced.

Fix: Run again; if it repeats, simplify the operation that crashes.

### POOL_CLOSED

The daemon is shutting down.

Fix: Start it again.

### INTERNAL_ERROR

Open3DJ failed in a way it did not expect, or a file system call failed with a code other than a path problem (the message names the code, such as ENOSPC). This is not a script error.

Fix: Run the same call again. If it repeats, check the disk (free space, permissions), then report it with the script.

## Examples

### Bracket with holes and rounded edges

One part with parameters, a batched cut and a fillet chosen by an edge query.

```js
const width = Param.number("Width", 60, { min: 30, max: 120, unit: "mm" });
const thick = Param.number("Thickness", 5, { min: 3, max: 12, unit: "mm" });
const size = Param.choice("Screw", "M4", ["M3", "M4", "M5"]);

const foot = box(width, 30, thick);
const wall = box(width, thick, 40).translate(0, 15 - thick / 2, 0);
const holes = [-1, 1].map((s) => lib.clearanceHole(size, { length: thick + 1 }).translate(s * (width / 2 - 10), -3, thick));
const bracket = foot.add(wall).subtract(holes);
return fillet(bracket, 1, { parallel: [1, 0, 0], minLength: width - 1 }).name("Bracket").color("#5b6b7a");
```

### Enclosure with a lid and four screws

Several parts in one assembly. The screws are clones, so they share one definition, and the lid is seated on the rim with connectors and matchTo.

```js
const W = 80, D = 60, H = 30, wall = 2.4, lidT = 4;
const corners = [[1, 1], [1, -1], [-1, 1], [-1, -1]].map(([sx, sy]) => [sx * (W / 2 - 7), sy * (D / 2 - 7)]);

const cavity = roundedRect(W - 2 * wall, D - 2 * wall, 2).extrude(H).translateZ(wall);
const bosses = corners.map(([x, y]) => cylinder(H - wall, 4.5).translate(x, y, wall));
const pockets = corners.map(([x, y]) => lib.heatSetPocket("M3").translate(x, y, H));
const body = roundedRect(W, D, 4).extrude(H).subtract(cavity).add(bosses).subtract(pockets)
  .withConnectors({ rim: connector.female("seat", { origin: [0, 0, H], axis: [0, 0, 1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) });

const holes = corners.map(([x, y]) => lib.clearanceHole("M3", { length: lidT + 1 }).translate(x, y, lidT));
const lid = roundedRect(W, D, 4).extrude(lidT).subtract(holes)
  .withConnectors({ under: connector.male("seat", { origin: [0, 0, 0], axis: [0, 0, -1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) })
  .matchTo(body, "under", "rim");

const screw = lib.bolt("M3", 8);
const screws = corners.map(([x, y]) => ({ name: "Screw", shape: screw.clone().translate(x, y, H + lidT) }));
return [{ name: "Body", shape: body, color: "#5b6b7a" }, { name: "Lid", shape: lid, color: "#00d4ff" }, ...screws];
```

### Turned knob from a revolved profile

A path profile revolved about Z, with a knurl made by a circular pattern of cuts.

```js
const profile = path().moveTo(0, 0).lineH(15).lineV(4).lineTo(13, 18).lineH(-13).close();
const knob = profile.revolve();
const grooves = circularPattern(cylinder(20, 1.2).translate(14.5, 0, 2), 18);
return knob.subtract(grooves).subtract(cylinder(12, 2.5).translate(0, 0, -1)).name("Knob");
```

## Gallery examples

The examples/ folder of the repository: tested parts and assemblies, with their measures in expected.json.

### box-with-lid

Two-part box: a shelled base and a lid with a locating lip. Script: examples/box-with-lid/box-with-lid.o3j.js.

```js
// Two-part box: a shelled base and a lid with a locating lip. Connectors seat the lid on
// the rim with matchTo, which records a fastened mate. The lip clears the inner wall by
// the Clearance parameter. Units are mm, Z is up.
const W = Param.number("Width", 70, { min: 40, max: 150, unit: "mm" });
const D = Param.number("Depth", 50, { min: 30, max: 120, unit: "mm" });
const H = Param.number("Height", 30, { min: 15, max: 80, unit: "mm" });
const gap = Param.number("Clearance", 0.25, { min: -1, max: 1, unit: "mm" });
const wall = 2, lidT = 3, lipH = 4, lipT = 1.6;

const base = roundedRect(W, D, 4).extrude(H).shell(wall)
  .withConnectors({ rim: connector.female("lid", { origin: [0, 0, H], axis: [0, 0, 1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) });

// The lid is built upside down from its seat: plate above Z = 0, lip below it.
const lipW = W - 2 * wall - 2 * gap, lipD = D - 2 * wall - 2 * gap, lipR = 2 - gap;
const lip = roundedRect(lipW, lipD, lipR).subtract(roundedRect(lipW - 2 * lipT, lipD - 2 * lipT, Math.max(lipR - lipT, 0.4)))
  .extrude(lipH).translateZ(-lipH);
const lid = roundedRect(W, D, 4).extrude(lidT).add(lip)
  .withConnectors({ seat: connector.male("lid", { origin: [0, 0, 0], axis: [0, 0, -1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) })
  .matchTo(base, "seat", "rim");

return [{ name: "Base", shape: base, color: "#5b6b7a" }, { name: "Lid", shape: lid, color: "#00a6d6" }];
```

### bracket

Corner bracket: an L-angle with a centre gusset, two clearance holes in each flange and rounded outer edges. Script: examples/bracket/bracket.o3j.js.

```js
// Corner bracket: an L-angle with a centre gusset, two clearance holes in each flange and
// rounded outer edges. One part. Units are mm, Z is up.
const W = Param.number("Width", 40, { min: 24, max: 100, unit: "mm" });
const L = Param.number("Leg", 35, { min: 20, max: 80, unit: "mm" });
const T = Param.number("Thickness", 4, { min: 2, max: 10, unit: "mm" });
const screw = Param.choice("Screw", "M4", ["M3", "M4", "M5"]);

// The base flange lies on Z = 0 and runs along +Y; the upright flange stands at Y = 0..T.
const base = box(W, L, T).translate(0, L / 2, 0);
const upright = box(W, T, L).translate(0, T / 2, 0);
// The gusset is drawn in the YZ plane (sketch X -> Y, sketch Y -> Z) and is T thick in X.
const gusset = polygon([[T, T], [L - 8, T], [T, L - 8]]).extrude(T).rotateX(90).rotateZ(90).translateX(-T / 2);

const xs = [-1, 1].map((s) => s * (W / 4 + T / 4));
const baseHoles = xs.map((x) => lib.clearanceHole(screw, { length: T + 1 }).translate(x, L * 0.62, T));
// Turn the downward cutter so it drills along -Y through the upright, from its inner face.
const wallHoles = xs.map((x) => lib.clearanceHole(screw, { length: T + 1 }).rotateX(-90).translate(x, T, L * 0.62));

const body = base.add(upright, gusset).subtract(baseHoles, wallHoles);
return fillet(body, 1, { parallel: [1, 0, 0], minLength: W - 0.5 }).name("Bracket").color("#5b6b7a");
```

### enclosure

Electronics enclosure: a base with corner bosses, M3 heat-set pockets and a cable hole; a lid with counterbored holes, seated on the rim by connectors; and four M3 x 6 socket head screws from lib, as clones of one screw. Script: examples/enclosure/enclosure.o3j.js.

```js
// Electronics enclosure: a base with corner bosses, M3 heat-set pockets and a cable hole;
// a lid with counterbored holes, seated on the rim by connectors; and four M3 x 6 socket
// head screws from lib, as clones of one screw. The screws end inside the pockets, so the
// fit check finds contacts and clearances but no clash. Units are mm, Z is up.
const W = Param.number("Width", 100, { min: 60, max: 180, unit: "mm" });
const D = Param.number("Depth", 70, { min: 50, max: 140, unit: "mm" });
const H = Param.number("Height", 32, { min: 20, max: 80, unit: "mm" });
const wall = 2.4, floor = 2.4, lidT = 4, inset = 6.5;
const corners = [[1, 1], [1, -1], [-1, 1], [-1, -1]].map(([sx, sy]) => [sx * (W / 2 - inset), sy * (D / 2 - inset)]);

const shellBody = roundedRect(W, D, 5).extrude(H)
  .subtract(roundedRect(W - 2 * wall, D - 2 * wall, 2.6).extrude(H).translateZ(floor));
const bosses = corners.map(([x, y]) => cylinder(H - floor, 4.5).translate(x, y, floor));
const pockets = corners.map(([x, y]) => lib.heatSetPocket("M3").translate(x, y, H));
const cableHole = cylinder(10, 4).pointAlong([1, 0, 0]).translate(-W / 2 - 1, 0, 14);
const base = shellBody.add(bosses).subtract(pockets, cableHole)
  .withConnectors({ rim: connector.female("lid", { origin: [0, 0, H], axis: [0, 0, 1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) });

// Counterbores sink the screw heads 3 mm into the 4 mm lid.
const bores = corners.map(([x, y]) => lib.screwCutter("M3", { head: "socket", length: lidT + 1 }).translate(x, y, lidT));
const lid = roundedRect(W, D, 5).extrude(lidT).subtract(bores)
  .withConnectors({ seat: connector.male("lid", { origin: [0, 0, 0], axis: [0, 0, -1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) })
  .matchTo(base, "seat", "rim");

// lib.bolt puts the head above Z = 0, so Z = 0 goes on the counterbore floor.
const screw = lib.bolt("M3", 6);
const headSeatZ = H + lidT - lib.fastener("M3").socketHead.k;
const screws = corners.map(([x, y]) => ({ name: "Screw", shape: screw.clone().translate(x, y, headSeatZ), color: "#202020" }));

return [{ name: "Base", shape: base, color: "#5b6b7a" }, { name: "Lid", shape: lid, color: "#a8dadc" }, ...screws];
```

### flange

Bolt flange: a disc with a raised hub, a centre bore, a circular pattern of M6 clearance holes and chamfered hub edges. Script: examples/flange/flange.o3j.js.

```js
// Bolt flange: a disc with a raised hub, a centre bore, a circular pattern of M6 clearance
// holes and chamfered hub edges. One part. Units are mm, Z is up.
const D = Param.number("Diameter", 80, { min: 50, max: 160, unit: "mm" });
const T = Param.number("Thickness", 8, { min: 4, max: 20, unit: "mm" });
const count = Param.number("Bolt holes", 6, { min: 3, max: 12, integer: true });
const hubH = 12, hubR = 16, boreR = 10;

const disc = cylinder(T, D / 2);
const hub = cylinder(T + hubH, hubR);
const bore = cylinder(T + hubH + 2, boreR).translateZ(-1);
const hole = lib.clearanceHole("M6", { length: T + 2 }).translate((D / 2 + hubR) / 2 + 2, 0, T + 1);
const body = disc.add(hub).subtract(bore, circularPattern(hole, count));

// Break the two circular edges on top of the hub: its outer rim and the bore.
return chamfer(body, 1, { atZ: T + hubH }).name("Flange").color("#8a8f98");
```

### hinge

Butt hinge: two leaves with alternating knuckles and a pin along X. Script: examples/hinge/hinge.o3j.js.

```js
// Butt hinge: two leaves with alternating knuckles and a pin along X. Knuckles clear each
// other by 0.4 mm and the pin clears its hole by 0.2 mm, so the fit check reports
// clearances only. Each leaf has two countersunk M3 holes. Units are mm, Z is up.
const L = Param.number("Length", 60, { min: 30, max: 120, unit: "mm" });
const knuckles = Param.number("Knuckles", 5, { min: 3, max: 9, integer: true });
const leafW = 20, t = 2.5, rK = 4, rPin = 1.5, rHole = 1.7, gap = 0.4;
const seg = L / knuckles;

// A cylinder along X from x0 to x1, centred on the hinge axis (Y = 0, Z = 0).
const rodX = (r, x0, x1) => cylinder(x1 - x0, r).pointAlong([1, 0, 0]).translateX(x0);

function leaf(side) {
  const plate = box(L, leafW - rK - gap, t).translate(0, side * (rK + gap + (leafW - rK - gap) / 2), -t / 2);
  const parts = [];
  for (let i = side < 0 ? 0 : 1; i < knuckles; i += 2) {
    const x0 = -L / 2 + i * seg + gap / 2, x1 = -L / 2 + (i + 1) * seg - gap / 2;
    parts.push(rodX(rK, x0, x1), box(x1 - x0, rK + gap, t).translate((x0 + x1) / 2, side * (rK + gap) / 2, -t / 2));
  }
  const holes = [-1, 1].map((s) => lib.screwCutter("M3", { head: "countersunk", length: t + 1 }).translate(s * L * 0.3, side * 13, t / 2));
  return plate.add(parts).subtract(rodX(rHole, -L / 2 - 1, L / 2 + 1), holes);
}

const pin = rodX(rPin, -L / 2, L / 2);
return [
  { name: "Leaf A", shape: leaf(-1), color: "#b08d57" },
  { name: "Leaf B", shape: leaf(1), color: "#c9a66b" },
  { name: "Pin", shape: pin, color: "#6c757d" },
];
```

### knob

Lathe-style knob: a revolved profile with a domed top, twelve grip flutes and a D-shaped bore for a 6 mm shaft. Script: examples/knob/knob.o3j.js.

```js
// Lathe-style knob: a revolved profile with a domed top, twelve grip flutes and a D-shaped
// bore for a 6 mm shaft. One part. Units are mm, Z is up.
const R = Param.number("Radius", 16, { min: 10, max: 30, unit: "mm" });
const H = Param.number("Height", 18, { min: 10, max: 40, unit: "mm" });
const flutes = Param.number("Flutes", 12, { min: 0, max: 24, integer: true });

// Sketch X is the radius and sketch Y the height. The top is a shallow arc centred on the
// axis, so it meets the axis square and the dome has a smooth pole (an arc that meets the
// axis at an angle makes a cone-like pole that STEP cannot carry).
const rimX = R - 3;
const domeR = (rimX * rimX + 4) / 4; // the circle through (rimX, H - 2) and (0, H) centred on the axis
const profile = path().moveTo(0, 0).lineH(R - 1).lineTo(R, 1).lineV(H - 5).lineTo(rimX, H - 2).arcTo(0, H, -domeR).close();
let knob = profile.revolve();

if (flutes > 0) {
  const flute = cylinder(H - 6, 1.6).translate(R + 0.6, 0, 2);
  knob = knob.subtract(circularPattern(flute, flutes));
}
// D bore: a 6 mm circle with a flat 1.5 mm from the axis, 12 mm deep from the bottom.
const dBore = cylinder(13, 3).translateZ(-1).intersect(box(6, 6, 14).translate(-1.5, 0, -1));
return knob.subtract(dBore).name("Knob").color("#2a9d8f");
```

### lid-interference

NEGATIVE TEST: the box-with-lid design with a lip 0.3 mm wider than the cavity on each side. Script: examples/lid-interference/lid-interference.o3j.js.

```js
// NEGATIVE TEST: the box-with-lid design with a lip 0.3 mm wider than the cavity on each
// side. The fit check must report the lid and base as a clash, and the run must end with
// status "warning". Units are mm, Z is up.
const W = Param.number("Width", 70, { min: 40, max: 150, unit: "mm" });
const D = Param.number("Depth", 50, { min: 30, max: 120, unit: "mm" });
const H = Param.number("Height", 30, { min: 15, max: 80, unit: "mm" });
const gap = Param.number("Clearance", -0.3, { min: -1, max: 1, unit: "mm" });
const wall = 2, lidT = 3, lipH = 4, lipT = 1.6;

const base = roundedRect(W, D, 4).extrude(H).shell(wall)
  .withConnectors({ rim: connector.female("lid", { origin: [0, 0, H], axis: [0, 0, 1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) });

// The lid is built upside down from its seat: plate above Z = 0, lip below it.
const lipW = W - 2 * wall - 2 * gap, lipD = D - 2 * wall - 2 * gap, lipR = 2 - gap;
const lip = roundedRect(lipW, lipD, lipR).subtract(roundedRect(lipW - 2 * lipT, lipD - 2 * lipT, Math.max(lipR - lipT, 0.4)))
  .extrude(lipH).translateZ(-lipH);
const lid = roundedRect(W, D, 4).extrude(lidT).add(lip)
  .withConnectors({ seat: connector.male("lid", { origin: [0, 0, 0], axis: [0, 0, -1], up: [1, 0, 0] }) })
  .matchTo(base, "seat", "rim");

return [{ name: "Base", shape: base, color: "#5b6b7a" }, { name: "Lid", shape: lid, color: "#00a6d6" }];
```

### phone-stand

Phone stand: a side profile extruded to width, with a front lip, a leaning backrest, a cable slot through the base and rounded long edges. Script: examples/phone-stand/phone-stand.o3j.js.

```js
// Phone stand: a side profile extruded to width, with a front lip, a leaning backrest, a
// cable slot through the base and rounded long edges. One part. Units are mm, Z is up.
const W = Param.number("Width", 70, { min: 50, max: 120, unit: "mm" });

// Side profile in (Y, Z): base plate, backrest leaning back, phone ledge and front lip.
const side = polygon([
  [0, 0], [95, 0], [95, 6], [40, 6], [68, 78], [61, 81], [30, 6], [12, 6], [12, 16], [4, 16], [0, 10],
]);
// Extrude along sketch Z, then turn it so sketch X -> Y, sketch Y -> Z and the extrusion -> X.
const body = side.extrude(W).rotateX(90).rotateZ(90).translateX(-W / 2);

// The slot stays 3 mm clear of the ledge corners, so their 1.5 mm fillets do not run into it.
const cableSlot = slot(12, 10).rotate(90).translate(0, 21).extrude(8).translateZ(-1);
const lipNotch = box(12, 14, 12).translate(0, 6, 9);
const stand = body.subtract(cableSlot, lipNotch);

return fillet(stand, 1.5, { parallel: [1, 0, 0], minLength: W - 0.5 }).name("Phone stand").color("#264653");
```

### tapered-cup

Tapered cup: a loft from a 60 mm circle at the base to a 76 mm circle at the rim. Script: examples/tapered-cup/tapered-cup.o3j.js.

```js
// Tapered cup: a loft from a 60 mm circle at the base to a 76 mm circle at the rim. The
// cavity is a second loft whose radius is one wall smaller at every height, so the side
// wall is 2.5 mm wide measured across. The base edge is rounded. Units are mm, Z is up.
const H = Param.number("Height", 70, { min: 30, max: 120, unit: "mm" });
const wall = Param.number("Wall", 2.5, { min: 1.2, max: 5, unit: "mm" });
const r0 = 30, r1 = 38;
const radiusAt = (z) => r0 + ((r1 - r0) * z) / H;

const outer = circle2d(r0).loftTo(circle2d(r1), H);
// The cavity starts one wall above the base and runs 1 mm past the rim to cut it open.
const cavity = circle2d(radiusAt(wall) - wall).loftTo(circle2d(radiusAt(H + 1) - wall), H + 1 - wall).translateZ(wall);
const cup = fillet(outer, 3, { atZ: 0 }).subtract(cavity);
return cup.name("Cup").color("#e07a5f");
```

### vented-box

Vented project box: an open tray hollowed with shell(), rows of vent slots through both long walls and four M3 mounting holes in the floor. Script: examples/vented-box/vented-box.o3j.js.

```js
// Vented project box: an open tray hollowed with shell(), rows of vent slots through both
// long walls and four M3 mounting holes in the floor. One part. Units are mm, Z is up.
const W = Param.number("Width", 90, { min: 60, max: 160, unit: "mm" });
const D = Param.number("Depth", 60, { min: 40, max: 120, unit: "mm" });
const H = Param.number("Height", 40, { min: 25, max: 80, unit: "mm" });
const wall = 2;

const tray = roundedRect(W, D, 6).extrude(H).shell(wall);

// One slot cutter lies along X and runs through both long walls along Y.
const slotCutter = slot(18, 3).extrude(D + 10).rotateX(90).translate(0, (D + 10) / 2, 12);
const column = linearPattern(slotCutter, 4, 0, 0, 6);
const vents = [-1, 0, 1].map((i) => column.clone().translateX(i * 24));

const holes = [[1, 1], [1, -1], [-1, 1], [-1, -1]].map(([sx, sy]) =>
  lib.clearanceHole("M3", { length: wall + 1 }).translate(sx * (W / 2 - 10), sy * (D / 2 - 10), wall));

return tray.subtract(vents, holes).name("Vented box").color("#3d405b");
```
